title: Private USDC Payments
summary: Confidential USDC balances with an auditor
description: Wraps USDC into an Encrypted ERC (eERC) converter: deposits turn public USDC into encrypted balances, transfers hide amounts on-chain, withdrawals turn it back, and a designated auditor can decrypt for compliance.
prompts: Pay salaries in USDC without showing amounts on-chain
Private USDC transfers with a compliance auditor
Make token balances confidential on Avalanche

checks.description: The converter is in converter mode
USDC is registered in the converter after the first deposit

review: The converter reuses the shared Fuji registrar, verifiers and BabyJubJub library from the registry; the verifiers match the circuits served at /eerc/circuits.
The auditor is registered before setAuditorPublicKey, and the builder knows the auditor can see every amount.
Ownership is two-step: the builder calls acceptOwnership, so the deployer never keeps control.
Key derivation and every proof run in the builder's browser through lib/eerc or @avalabs/ac-eerc-sdk; nothing secret reaches the server.
Deposits and withdrawals are public by nature; only balances and transfer amounts are hidden.

frontend.summary: A private USDC wallet: deposit USDC, pay other members without amounts showing on-chain, and withdraw back.
audience: People paying or getting paid in USDC without showing amounts publicly
An auditor who must be able to see amounts
journeys: Set up once with a wallet signature, framed as creating your private account.
Deposit USDC into your private balance; amounts are in cents, and any dust that can't be made private is shown and returned.
Pay a member privately: recipient, amount, a clear 'creating a privacy proof' step with its expected time, then done.
Say plainly what stays private (amounts and balances) and what doesn't (who deposits and withdraws, and that the auditor sees amounts).
Auditor view, only with the auditor key: payments with their decrypted amounts.
flows: Load the eerc skill and start from its templates; every screen uses useEERC('EncryptedERC', { token: USDC address from useTokens }).
Everything happens in the app: never link users to Builder Hub's eERC console to register, deposit, pay, withdraw or see a balance.
Deposit: deposit(amount) approves USDC when needed and makes it private; show the wallet's USDC balance beside the form and say dust below 0.01 is returned.
Pay: isRegistered(to), then transfer(to, amount) with stageText while the proof is generated.
Withdraw: withdraw(amount) back to public USDC, saying the withdrawn amount becomes public.
Auditor tab: decrypt the auditor ciphertexts from PrivateTransfer events with the auditor's key, as components/toolbox/console/encrypted-erc/AuditorView.tsx does.
